Network guides

Step-by-step explanations with worked examples, written for working engineers and exam students.

Guide

How Subnetting Works

Learn how subnetting works with a clear step-by-step method: network and host bits, subnet masks, block size and a fully worked example for 192.168.10.77/26.

Guide

How Many Hosts Are in a Subnet?

Calculate usable hosts in any IPv4 subnet with 2^n minus 2. Includes a /8 to /32 table, the /31 and /32 exceptions and how to choose a prefix for a host count.

Guide

CIDR Notation Explained

CIDR notation explained clearly: what the slash number means, why it replaced classful addressing, how route aggregation works and how routers pick the longest prefix.

Guide

VLSM Tutorial

A step-by-step VLSM tutorial. Learn to allocate variable length subnets from one address block, with a worked example that fits four segments into a /24.

Guide

Wildcard Masks Explained

Learn what a wildcard mask is, how to calculate one from a subnet mask, and how to use it in Cisco ACLs and OSPF network statements, with worked examples.

Guide

Private IP Address Ranges

The three private IPv4 ranges in RFC 1918, plus CGNAT, link-local, loopback and IPv6 unique local addresses, with sizes and guidance on which to choose.

Guide

IPv4 vs IPv6 Subnetting

How IPv6 subnetting differs from IPv4: the /64 rule, no broadcast addresses, hexadecimal prefixes, and how to plan /48 and /56 allocations.

Guide

Common Subnet Sizes and When to Use Them

A quick reference of common IPv4 subnet sizes from /16 to /32 with masks, address counts, usable hosts and the situations where each size is normally used.

Guide

BGP, ASNs and RPKI Explained

What an autonomous system number is, how BGP uses it to exchange routes, how to read an AS path, and how RPKI route origin validation protects against route hijacks.

Guide

DNS Record Types Explained

A plain-language guide to the common DNS record types, what each one does, and an example of how it looks in a zone file.

Guide

Bandwidth-Delay Product and TCP Throughput

Why a fast link can still give slow transfers. Learn the bandwidth-delay product, how the TCP window limits throughput, and how to calculate the window you need.

Guide

Public vs Private IP Addresses and NAT

The difference between public and private IP addresses, how NAT and PAT let private hosts reach the internet, and the common problems NAT causes.

Each guide has worked examples and links to the matching calculator.
